title: Hourly Bookkeeper — Interior Design (Canada) & Short-Term Rental Management (US) — Part-Time
description:
I am looking for a reliable, detail-oriented bookkeeper to support two small, early-stage companies on an hourly basis.



One company, based in Canada, provides interior design services. The other, based in the US, provides short-term rental management. Both are just getting started, with a growth plan beginning next year.



This is a very light role to start — just a few hours per month — with room to expand as both businesses grow.



What you'll do:



For both companies, keeping the books separate:



Categorize transactions and reconcile bank and credit card accounts

Track income, expenses, and invoices

Prepare simple monthly summaries and reports

Organize receipts and records for year-end and for our accountant

Flag anything that looks off or needs attention



For the Canadian interior design company:

Manage client and project invoicing, and supplier/vendor bills

Help with CRA remittances, including GST and BC PST where applicable



For the US short-term rental management company:

Track rental income, platform payouts, management fees, and cleaning costs

Reconcile owner statements and property-related expenses



What we're looking for:

- Experience with Canadian bookkeeping, including federal and British Columbia requirements

- Familiarity with GST and PST in BC

- Experience with US short-term rental bookkeeping strongly preferred, including platform payouts and rental income tracking

- Comfort working across CAD and USD, and keeping two companies' books separate

- Experience with Xero and Wave accounting

Strong attention to detail, good communication, and discretion with financial information

- Able to work independently and meet monthly deadlines

- Able to do regular, frequent zoom call with manager



Details:

- Hourly, part-time, and flexible 

- Remote, within Canada or the US preferred

- Start date: ASAP

- Hours are expected to grow next year as both businesses expand



To apply:

Please send a brief introduction, your relevant experience with Canadian / BC and US bookkeeping and short-term rental bookkeeping, your hourly rate, and your availability.

description:
We run a local clinic where every conversion starts with a phone call.

Manage and optimize Google Ads Search campaigns

Identify and eliminate wasted spend from search terms

Improve call quality — not just call volume

Align ads and landing pages with real caller intent

Diagnose whether problems come from traffic quality, tracking gaps, landing pages, or call handling

Fewer junk calls, higher percentage of qualified calls

Higher booking rate per call

Clear thinking and fast decisions

Direct communication — no fluff

Proven experience with Google Ads Search for local lead generation

Experience with call-driven accounts where not every caller is a qualified lead

Strong grasp of search terms, negative keyword strategy, match types, and geo and device performance

Ability to act, not just analyze

To Apply

What type of accounts you've managed and roughly how long

One call-driven account you've worked on — what the main problem was and what you did about it

At least 3 project references (client websites) that you personally worked on. Please do not submit agency portfolio websites or projects you did not directly manage.

Your availability for a short Zoom call



Next step

Qualified applicants will be invited to a live Zoom session where we walk through real account scenarios together. No presentations, no decks. Just a conversation about how you think.

title: Ticket Broker Specialist
description:
Seat Vantage Group is looking for an experienced Ticket Brokerage Operations Specialist with at least 3 years of experience working for a ticket brokerage or ticket resale company.



This is not an entry-level position. We are looking for someone who understands the ticket brokerage industry and can assist with ticket purchasing, inventory management, marketplace operations, and other day-to-day brokerage activities.



Requirements:



* Minimum 3 years of ticket brokerage experience

* Experience with Jancy, Primo, AYCD, or similar ticket purchasing/automation tools

* Strong understanding of Ticketmaster, AXS, Live Nation, SeatGeek, and other ticketing platforms

* Understanding of marketplaces such as StubHub, Vivid Seats, SeatGeek, GameTime, GoTickets, and TicketNetwork

* Strong organizational and communication skills

* Highly ambitious, competitive, and results-driven

Responsibilities:



* Assist with ticket purchasing during on-sales

* Maintain and update ticket inventory

* Assist with marketplace listings and pricing updates

* Track purchases, sales, transfers, and deliveries

* Support daily brokerage operations and administrative tasks

* Help identify profitable opportunities and improve operational efficiency

title: YouTube Script Writer and Researcher - 10-15 Minute Breakdowns of Viral Public Incidents
description:
We're hiring a writer who is also a strong researcher to script long-form YouTube videos about viral public i
. These are the "Karen" confrontations you see on TikTok and Instagram: road rage, parking lots, flights, restaurants and stores. Each video tells one story from start to finish: what happened on camera, who the person turned out to be, how they explained themselves, and what it cost them, from losing a job to criminal charges. Videos run 8–15 minutes. We're looking for someone to work with us on an ongoing basis.



The research matters as much as the writing. Every fact in a script must come from a source you can link, and anything that is only one person's claim has to be presented as a claim.



WHAT YOU'LL DO



- Find stories. Each week, pitch 3–5 viral i
 where the person has been publicly identified and has faced consequences, with links. Sources include TikTok, Instagram, X, Reddit, local news and commentary channels.



- Research each approved story into a timeline: the original clip and who posted it, how the person was identified, their apology or excuse, employer statements, police reports, court records and charges, and any updates since.



- Check everything. Confirm identities through news reports or the person's own response, never a guess from the comments. Tell proven facts apart from claims, and say what is still unknown.



- Write the script to be read aloud, in the order below. Mark every point where a clip plays, with the clip's link and timestamps.



- Include a source list with every script: a link for each fact.



- Track stories you've written about and flag new developments for follow-up videos, such as court dates, lawsuits and new statements.



HOW EACH SCRIPT IS BUILT



1. Cold open: the most shocking few seconds of the clip.

2. Hook: one or two sentences that sum up the i
 and tease the consequences.

3. Context: the exact date, time, place and business, who filmed it and what happened before the recording started.

4. The clip, then a short explanation of what we just watched.

5. Who they are: name, age and job as reported, and who identified them.

6. Their side: the apology, statement or excuse, checked against the evidence.

7. The consequences: firing, charges, bail and court dates, business reviews.

8. Closing line: a sharp callback to something earlier in the story.



EXAMPLE OPENING (an imaginary story, to show the style)



[CLIP 0:04–0:09: "It's two dollars! Two!"]

So, you're working the Saturday shift at a self-serve car wash, and a man in a brand-new pickup d
 the token machine has robbed him. Of two dollars. By the end of the afternoon he's hit a 17-year-old attendant with a pressure washer, and by Monday his own company has put out a statement about him. It's March 8th, at a car wash in Mesa, Arizona. The attendant, Jordan, is restocking towels when the man waves him over. Take a look.

[CLIP 0:00–0:52]

According to the police report, the attendant asked him to step back from the machine twice before the hose came up.



The tone is conversational and dry, never shouty, and always on the side of the person being harassed. The humour comes from specific details, not insults.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



- Excellent written English that sounds natural to an American audience when read aloud.



- Real research skills. You can find and read news reports, court record searches, police statements and company announcements, and you know a primary source from a repost.



- Accuracy and care. You attribute claims ("she says", "according to police"), call charges charges and not convictions, and never state a guess as fact.



- Storytelling. You can turn a messy timeline into a script that keeps people watching to the end.



- A dry sense of humour that comes from details, not name-calling.



- Comfort with heated footage, including swearing and racial slurs. Scripts describe slurs and never repeat them.



- Good judgement about privacy. Scripts never include home addresses, phone numbers or details about family members or children.



- Reliable deadlines.



- Bonus: experience writing or researching for YouTube commentary, true crime or news channels, or you already watch channels like That Danesh Guy.



Workload: To start, 2 scripts a week, each about 1,200–2,000 words, plus weekly story pitches.



Turnaround: Each script is due within 3 days of its story being approved.



HOW TO APPLY



Start your application with the word "papaya" and include:



1. Your
 address



2. Links to 1–3 scripts or long-form pieces you've written (Google Docs set so anyone with the link can view)



3. Links to any YouTube channels or videos you've written or researched for, what you did and when (or "none yet")



4. A short research sample: pick a viral public i
 from the last 6 months where the person was identified and faced consequences, and give its timeline in 5–8 bullet points with a source link for each point



5. A sample opening for that same i
 (60–100 words), written to be read aloud



6. Your expected rate (per script of about 1,500 words, or per month)



7. How many scripts a week you can take on, and your usual working hours (Philippine time)



8. Your

Applications that skip the code word or any of items 1–7 won't be reviewed.

title: Clip Editor – Stream Clips to Vertical Shorts for TikTok, Reels & YouTube Shorts (50-100+ clips/week, ongoing, remote)
description:
I send you clips from a streamer’s channel, and you turn them into polished vertical shorts for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other platforms. The clips are already picked. Your job is to trim, frame, caption, and export. This is ongoing weekly work for the right person.



THE JOB



You’ll get a sheet of clip links from the streamer’s clips page, with IN/OUT points within each clip and the line being clipped

50+ clips per week, delivered in batches of 10–15

One export per clip works across TikTok, Reels, and Shorts

Expected pace: about 10 clips per hour once you’re set up. If a clip takes you 20 minutes, this isn’t the right fit.



OUTPUT SPECS



9:16 vertical, exported at 1080×1920

Always crop to fill, never letterbox. Scaling the crop up to 1080×1920 is expected.

Layout: [facecam only / facecam stacked over gameplay]. A reference clip is provided.

Length: 15–50 seconds

Captions: burned in, 2–4 words per line, high contrast, [font / color / position]. A template is provided.

Keep captions and faces inside platform safe zones, clear of the TikTok/Reels buttons and caption area

Audio normalized to [-14 LUFS]

Export: MP4, H.264, [30/60] fps



QUALITY BAR



Cuts land within 0.5s of the IN/OUT points. Use that window to start and end on a clean word. Mid-word openings are the most common rejection.

The hook is visible in the first 1.5 seconds. If the clip doesn’t allow that, flag it in your batch notes instead of guessing.

Framing is head-and-chest, centered in the upper part of the frame, never cropped at the eyes. Any exceptions will be noted in the sheet.

Captions match the audio exactly. Fix auto-caption errors on names, slang, game terms, and crosstalk. A glossary of names and terms is provided.

Flag any clip that’s missing its setup, has muted audio, or is too low quality to use.



WHAT TO CUT AROUND



Ads, sponsor reads, or brand promo segments

BRB screens, countdowns, intro stings, or raid shoutouts

Dead air. Five seconds of silence in a clip means it’s wrong.



If any of these fall inside a clip, remove them with a clean jump cut, or flag the clip if removing them breaks it.



PAY AND TERMS



Paid test batch: 10 clips (about 1 hour) at $3.35/hour

Ongoing: $3.25–4.50/hour, about 10-15 hours per week for 50-100+ clips (roughly $150–250/month)

Hours tracked per batch [time tracker / reported hours]

Paid every Friday via PayPal, crypto or others.

One revision round per clip.

24-hour turnaround per batch



REQUIREMENTS



Video editing experience, with a portfolio of short-form vertical work (TikTok, Reels, or Shorts)

A computer that can smoothly edit and export 1080p footage

Editing software that supports reframing, burned-in captions, and audio normalization (Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut desktop, or similar)

A reliable internet connection for downloading clips and uploading batches on time

Familiarity with platform safe zones and short-form caption styles

Clear, responsive communication

title: Software User Tester (US Real Estate App) - Full-Time, 40 hrs/week, $3.50/hr
description:
THE JOB IN ONE SENTENCE



Use Lot Decoder all day, in every US state, the way real agents, investors and builders do, and find every wrong answer, broken screen and confusing word before our users do.



- Hours: full time, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday

- Pay: $3.50/hr, as an independent contractor

- Where: remote, Philippines-based

- Team: you find the problems. A Zoning Reviewer fixes zoning numbers and a Price Accuracy Checker fixes prices. Everything else goes to the owner.



WHAT IS LOT DECODER?



Agents, investors and builders type in an address. Lot Decoder tells them what they can build on that lot and what it might cost and earn, in any US city. Deal Finder searches a whole city for empty lots that could make money. If any of that is wrong, someone could lose real money on a bad deal. Your job is to find it first.



WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU



This is a high-output role. These are the numbers you'll be measured on every week.



- Deal Finder searches: Weeks 1–2: 60 a week; Weeks 3–4: 80 a week; Week 5 on: 100 a week

- Full reports opened and checked: Weeks 1–2: 20 a week; Weeks 3–4: 35 a week; Week 5 on: 50 a week

- Different US states covered: Weeks 1–2: 3 a week; Weeks 3–4: 4 a week; Week 5 on: 5 a week (all 50 states in about 10 weeks)

- Confirmed defects filed: Weeks 1–2: 15 a week; Weeks 3–4: 25 a week; Week 5 on: 30 a week

- Defects the owner can repeat from your steps: 90%

- Fixed defects re-tested: within 1 business day

- Stop-ship defects reported: within 1 hour



What counts as a confirmed defect: a real problem that someone else can see by following your steps. Duplicates, guesses and "I think this might be wrong" without proof don't count. One real wrong-money defect is worth more than ten typos.



As the app gets better, defects get harder to find. The defect target will be reset with you every month so it stays tough but fair.



Missing the weekly targets two weeks in a row means we talk about whether the role is a fit.



YOUR DAILY ROUTINE



Step 1: Start of day (15 minutes)



1. Open the Team page (
/#/team), pick "Test plan" and tap Clock in. Your hours count automatically from here.

2. Open the Defects card. Re-test every report marked Fixed (see "How to re-test a fix" below).

3. Read "Test plan for today" on the Team page: today's new city, the repeat city and the focus. Tap Next to open Deal Finder already set to that city.



Step 2: Run Deal Finder searches (about 3 hours)



Run 20 searches a day: 1 or 2 in today's new city, and the rest as repeats in cities already searched (try a different ZIP code, lot size or development type). Repeats cost us much less and still test the app. If you see "today's budget reached", move on to Step 4. For each search:



1. Open Deal Finder in Lot Decoder and type the place from your test plan.

2. Time it. Write down how long until the first lots show, and how long until the search finishes.

3. Check the top 5 cards and 2 random cards from lower down. For each card, check:

   - Is it a real, empty lot? Open the map or aerial photo. A house, building or parking lot on it is a defect.

   - Is it in the place you searched? A lot from another city or ZIP code is a defect.

   - Is it really for sale (for-sale cards)? Open the listing link. Sold, pending or a dead link is a defect.

   - Is it government land? Owner names like "City of...", "County of...", "State of..." or "Housing Authority" are defects.

   - Does the zoning label make sense? Compare the card's zone with the county's official zoning map. A different zone is a Zoning defect.

   - Do the owner and mailing details make sense (off-market cards)?

   - Does every link and button work?

   - Can a first-time user understand every word? Anything confusing is a Wording defect.



Step 3: Open full reports (about 3 hours)



Open 10 reports a day, all from lots in that day's Deal Finder results: 5 by clicking the card, and 5 by typing that lot's address into the home page.



For each report:



1. Check the lot: is the outline on the map the right lot? Is the address right?

2. Check the zoning numbers (lot size, height, setbacks) against the county zoning map and the city code. File any that look wrong as Zoning defects with the code link.

3. Check the sales the report used: are they real sales nearby, of the same property type the report plans to build (house, townhome, condo, apartments, retail or industrial)? Any that are far away or a different type go in as Price defects. If the finished sale price looks far above or below similar sold properties nearby, file it as a Price defect too. Don't do the full price check yourself; the Price Checker does that.

4. Read every sentence. Anything that contradicts another part of the report, or that a beginner wouldn't understand, is a defect.

5. Try every button: save, share, presentations, offer letter and contact owner. Don't send anything to a real owner, agent or customer.



Step 4: Try to break it (about 1 hour)



Every day, try 5 things a real user might do by mistake:



- type an address with a typo, no city, or a unit number

- search a tiny town, a rural county, or a place with no empty lots

- use your phone in portrait and landscape

- go back, refresh or switch tabs in the middle of a search

- run two searches at once in two tabs



Step 5: File every defect the same day



Every defect gets one report: tap "Something look wrong? Report a problem" at the bottom of the page, on the page where you found it. See "How to file a defect" below. File Stop-ship defects within 1 hour, and also message Debbie in Skool right away.



Step 6: End of day (5 minutes)



1. On the Team page, tap Clock out. Your hours, searches, reports and defects are counted automatically and show in the Team feed.

2. Message Debbie in Skool with 2 lines: the worst thing you found today, and anything blocking you.



HOW TO FILE A DEFECT



One report per problem. Write these in the report box, one per line, and tap "Add a screenshot".



- Date: Today's date

- Type: Zoning, Price, Wrong lot, Not empty, Not for sale, Government land, Slow, Broken, Wording, Other

- Severity: Stop-ship: wrong money, wrong lot, a crash, or something a user could lose money on. Major: wrong information that a careful user might catch. Minor: wording, layout or a small glitch.

- Where: The full address or place searched, and the page link

- Steps: Numbered steps someone else can follow to see it

- Expected: What should have happened

- What happened: What actually happened, with the exact numbers or words

- Proof: A screenshot, plus a link to the official source (zoning map, code, sold listing)

- Device: Phone or computer, and the browser



Where it goes: Zoning defects go to the Zoning Reviewer, Price defects go to the Price Accuracy Checker, and everything else goes to the owner. The Type you write routes it. You don't need to message anyone except for Stop-ship defects.



Before filing: check the Defects card for the same address or problem. If it's already there, don't file it twice.



HOW TO RE-TEST A FIX



1. Follow the report's Steps exactly.

2. If the problem is gone, mark it Passed in the Defects card.

3. If it's still there, mark it Failed and file a new report with a new screenshot that mentions the first one.

4. Also check one other place with the same kind of problem (another city, another lot). If it shows up there, file a new report and mention the first one. Fixes must work everywhere, not just on one address.



RULES



1. Never contact a real owner, seller, agent or customer. Contact tools are tested only up to the final send button.

2. Use only the test account the owner gives you, and stay under the daily search limit. Searches cost real money.

3. Proof beats opinion. Every Zoning or Price defect needs an official link or a real sold listing.

4. Report what you see, not what you guess the cause is.

5. Keep everything confidential: the app, its numbers, and every defect report.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



- You've done software testing (QA), or you've worked in US real estate support and are relentlessly detail-minded.

- You know how to read a US county parcel map or a listing, or can learn it in your first week.

- You write steps so clearly that someone else can repeat them the first time.

- You stay sharp doing the same kind of check 100 times a week.

- A plus: experience with US zoning maps, US real estate, or testing mobile apps.



TRAINING IN YOUR FIRST 30 DAYS (PAID)



1. Finish all 8 Lot Decoder courses and their quizzes in our Skool community within your first 30 days.

2. Be active in the community: introduce yourself, then make at least 3 helpful posts or replies a week.

3. Course time is paid at your normal hourly rate once your access is on. On the Team page, pick "Training" when you clock in. Studying before your access is on is optional and unpaid.

4. In the community, label yourself as "Lot Decoder Team". Never pose as a customer.



HOW IT STARTS



1. Paid trial: 4 hours on the live app, paid at $3.50/hr. File as many confirmed defects as you can. We grade every one.

2. 90 days: we review your defect count, quality and weekly targets together.

3. Contract: independent contractor agreement with confidentiality and work-for-hire terms.



TO APPLY



Send:



1. A few lines about your testing or real estate experience.

2. Confirm that $3.50/hr for 40 hours a week works for you.

3. One defect you found in any website or app, written with Steps, Expected and What happened.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with numbers, spreadsheets, suppliers and systems, and takes pride in accuracy and efficiency.



Your Responsibilities



Prepare, process and track purchase orders.



Liaise with Australian and international suppliers regarding orders, pricing and deliveries.



Monitor stock levels, backorders and replenishment requirements.



Help identify products that need reordering and highlight slow-moving stock.



Maintain accurate supplier, product and pricing records.



Prepare purchasing, inventory and sales reports.



Analyse data using Excel, including formulas, lookups and PivotTables.



Track shipments and follow up on outstanding orders.



Identify discrepancies and work with the team to resolve them.



Assist with sourcing new products and suppliers.



What We're Looking For



Previous experience in purchasing, procurement, inventory or supply chain administration.



Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including PivotTables and lookup formulas — essential.



Excellent attention to detail and numerical accuracy.



Experience using inventory, purchasing or ERP software.



Strong written and spoken English.



Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.



Confidence working independently and communicating with a remote team.



A proactive approach to solving problems.



Experience with NetSuite, international purchasing or wholesale distribution would be a strong advantage.



What We Offer



Stable, long-term full-time employment.



Work-from-home flexibility.



A supportive Australian team.



Training on our internal systems and processes.



Opportunities to take on more responsibility as you develop.



Competitive salary based on experience.



How to Apply



Please send your resume and briefly answer the following:



What purchasing or inventory experience do you have?



How confident are you using Excel PivotTables and lookup formulas?



Which inventory or ERP systems have you previously used?



What monthly salary are you seeking in PHP?



Shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a short Excel assessment.

title: Online English/World History Teachers (Near-Native Accent)
description:
About Pomelo Academy

Pomelo Academy is an innovative online international school dedicated to delivering high-quality education to students worldwide. We provide a dynamic and engaging learning environment, catering to individualized instruction that transcends geographical boundaries.



Job Description

We are seeking passionate and experienced Near-Native English-speaking Online K-12 Math and/or Science Teachers with verifiable teaching certifications. The ideal candidates will have strong academic backgrounds in Mathematics and/or Science, experience teaching young learners (ages 5–18), and a commitment to creating a supportive, inquiry-based, and engaging online learning environment.



Responsibilities



Deliver interactive and engaging Math and/or Science lessons to individuals and small groups of 2–6 students aged 5–18.

Teach using internationally recognized curricula such as A Closer Look, Glencoe Science, Pearson Interactive Science, NGSS-aligned resources, Singapore Math, or IB/AP/A Level Math programs.

Create age-appropriate lesson plans focused on conceptual understanding, inquiry, problem-solving, and real-world applications.

Incorporate visuals, multimedia, and hands-on virtual activities to make abstract concepts accessible and engaging.

Monitor student progress and provide timely feedback to students and parents.

Foster curiosity, discussion, and active learning in a safe and supportive space.



Qualifications



Professional teacher with at least 2 years of teaching experience (Kindergarten–Grade 12).

Must hold a valid teaching license/certification (e.g., Teaching License, State Certification). TESOL/TEFL is a plus.

Near-native English accent with excellent spoken and written communication skills.

Strong academic background in Mathematics and/or Science (Biology, Physics, Chemistry, General Science).

Experience teaching in public/international schools or reputable online platforms.

Familiarity with inquiry-based and/or interdisciplinary approaches (e.g., STEM/STEAM).

Comfortable working between 07:00–22:00 (Weekdays) and 9:00–22:00 (Weekends), GMT+8.

Proficiency with digital platforms such as ClassIn, Microsoft Office, and other educational technologies.

Must have a stable and fast internet connection and a PC/laptop with at least Windows 10 or Mac OS Catalina.



Benefits



Flexible working hours.

Opportunity to teach using globally respected Math and Science curricula.

Be part of an international, passionate team of educators.

Access to training and professional development.

Regular enrollment model (not a booking system), ensuring schedule stability and consistency

title: Operations Assistant
description:
Operations Assistant



Location: Remote – Philippines  

Hours: Full-time | 40 hours per week | 5pm–2am Philippines time (aligned with UK working hours)  

Salary: £500–£700 per month, depending on experience and skillset, plus performance bonus and paid UK bank holidays.



About Innermost:



At Innermost, we believe better health comes from finding the right balance between nature and science. Inspired by traditional ingredients and powered by modern, evidence-based research, we've developed a fresh approach to wellness. We combine natural ingredients with cutting-edge science to create products that are effective, transparent and rooted in quality. Our mission is simple: to make better health easy. Founded in London, Innermost has experienced significant growth since launch, and we have ambitious plans for the future. We're building a challenger brand with the ambition to change the way people think about health and wellness. If you'd like to be part of a growing international business and contribute to something ambitious, we'd love to hear from you. Learn more at 



The Role:



We're looking for a highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented Operations Assistant to join our growing team. This is a varied role covering multiple areas of the business, including finance, accounting, supply chain, inventory management, reporting and customer experience. You'll join our existing Operations team, working alongside four other team members who are based remotely in the Philippines and support the day-to-day running of our international business.



This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems and working across different areas of a business. You'll need to be comfortable managing multiple priorities, working independently and taking responsibility for ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time.



Key Responsibilities:



Operations >>



- Executing daily, weekly and monthly operational tasks to ensure the smooth running of the business.

- Supporting the coordination and management of internal processes and workflows.

- Identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and streamline processes.



Finance & Accounting >>



- Bookkeeping and maintaining accurate financial records.

- Bank and account reconciliations.

- Managing accounts payable and receivable.

- Supporting financial administration and reporting.



Inventory & Supply Chain >>



- Monitoring inventory levels across products and warehouses.

- Coordinating stock replenishment orders and monitoring deliveries.

- Maintaining accurate inventory records and identifying potential stock shortages.

- Supporting supplier and logistics coordination.



Customer Experience >>



- Managing customer enquiries and providing timely, professional responses.

- Resolving customer issues and escalating matters where necessary.

- Supporting customer retention and customer success initiatives.

- Ensuring customers receive a consistently positive experience.



Reporting & Data Management >>



- Assisting with weekly and monthly management reporting.

- Maintaining spreadsheets, databases and operational records.

- Analysing data and helping identify trends, discrepancies and opportunities for improvement.



Skills & Experience:



- A degree in Business, Management, Finance, Accounting or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

- Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

- Excellent numerical and analytical abilities.

- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including Pivot Tables, lookup functions, SUMIFS and working with larger datasets.

- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

- Ability to work independently, take initiative and solve problems without constant supervision.

- A proactive approach to work, with a willingness to take ownership and responsibility.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambitious environment with high expectations.

- A positive attitude and willingness to support colleagues and contribute to a team.



Additional Information:



This is a full-time position requiring 40 working hours per week, spread across five days (eight working hours per day, plus a one-hour break). Salary of £500–£700 per month, depending on experience, qualifications and skillset. In addition, you will receive an end-of-year performance bonus and paid time off for eight UK bank holidays, despite not being required to work on those days. Innermost is based in London, United Kingdom, and our core working hours are 9am–6pm UK time. The corresponding Philippines working hours are generally 5pm–2am.



How to Apply:



We'd love to hear from candidates who believe they have the skills, experience and attitude to succeed in this role. Please submit your CV along with some additional information about your experience and skillset. We'd also like you to record a short 60-second video explaining why you believe you'd be a good fit for the position and what you could bring to the team.



Please also answer the following questions when applying:



1. Where do you currently live? Please specify whether you live in a city or a village.

2. What is your internet connection speed, and do you have reliable electricity in your area?

3. What IT equipment do you have available to support your work? For example, Macbook, laptop or desktop computer, additional monitor, headset and backup internet connection.



Please submit your application through the OnlineJobs.ph messaging platform and include a link to your video recording (Loom is preferred). Shortlisted candidates will be contacted regarding the next steps, which may include an interview over Zoom.



**Please follow the application instructions carefully. Applications that do not include the requested information and video may not be considered.**



Thank you, and we look forward to hearing from you.
